# RFC reference audit results
## Summary
- Cross-checked every `RFC 7530 §X` citation in the repository (95+ sites) against the actual table of contents and body text of `docs/rfc7530.txt`. - Most common error pattern: **using the NFSv4 op number directly as the §16 section number**. RFC 7530's `§16.N` is *not* indexed by op number — operation N (3 ≤ N ≤ 39) lives in `§16.(N-2)` (e.g. ACCESS = op 3 / §16.1, CLOSE = op 4 / §16.2, COMMIT = op 5 / §16.3, …). - Citations that happened to land on the right section (READ §16.23, WRITE §16.36, OPEN §16.16, etc.) were left alone; only the misaligned ones were corrected. - Other corrections cover **wrong-chapter** citations (e.g. claiming `stateid4` lives in §3.3 / §8.1) and a handful of citations to subsections that **do not exist at all** (e.g. §3.3.5, §3.3.13, §5.11). - `swift build` confirmed green throughout.
## Catalogue of corrected hallucinations / misattributions
### 1. CompoundDispatcher.swift — the most heavily off-by-N file

COMPOUND is a *procedure*, hence §15.2. | | line 22 | `§16.2.4` (tag) | `§15.2.4` | Tag definition is in COMPOUND DESCRIPTION. | | line 53 | `§16.2.4: tag has no length cap` | `§15.2.4: …` | Same as above. | | line 64 | `§16.2.5 — minorversion mismatch` | `§15.2.4 — minorversion mismatch` | The `MINOR_VERS_MISMATCH` rule is stated in §15.2.4. | | line 149 | `§16.20` (PUTPUBFH) | `§16.21 (PUTPUBFH)` | §16.20 is PUTFH; PUTPUBFH is §16.21. | | line 165 | `Filehandle ops (§16.20-§16.31)` | `§16.8 GETFH, §16.20-§16.22, §16.29-§16.30 …` | The 16.20-31 range mostly contains unrelated ops (READ/READDIR/REMOVE, etc.). ### 2. NFSv4Constants.swift
- `// RFC 7530 §16.1 — operation opcodes (nfs_opnum4).` → corrected to `§14.4 / §16`. §16.1 is just one op (ACCESS); the op-number definition lives in §14.4 "Operation Values" + §16 as a whole.
### 3. FATTR4.swift
- `LEASE_TIME (§5.6)` → `§5.8.1.11`. §5.6 is the REQUIRED-attrs table header; the actual definition is §5.8.1.11. - `silently dropped from the response (§16.18 — GETATTR)` → `§16.7 — GETATTR`. §16.18 is OPEN_CONFIRM. - `changeid4 (§5.7)` → `§5.8.1.4 (change attr) / §2.1 changeid4`. §5.7 is the RECOMMENDED-attrs table. - `nfstime4 (§2.2.4)` → `§2.2.1`. §2.2.4 is `specdata4`.
### 4. SetattrDecoder.swift
- `settime4 (§5.9)` → `§2.2.3`. §5.9 is owner / owner_group interpretation. `settime4` is defined in §2.2.3.
### 5. RPCSession.swift
- `§3.2.1 + AUTH_SYS` → `§3.2`. §3.2.1 is RPCSEC_GSS / Kerberos; the place where AUTH_SYS is mentioned is §3.2 (Security Flavors).
### 6. NFSError.swift
- `case wrongType // NFS4ERR_WRONG_TYPE = 10083 (§13.1.1)` → `mapped to NFS4ERR_BADTYPE = 10007 (§13.1.4.1)`. **`NFS4ERR_WRONG_TYPE` does not exist in RFC 7530** (it was added in NFSv4.1 / RFC 5661). The code's `wrongType` case is mapped to `NFS4ERR_BADTYPE` on the wire via `asStatus`, so the comment was rewritten to match the wire reality.
### 7. NFSAccess.swift
- `MARK: Access (§16.3 ACCESS)` → `§16.1 ACCESS`. §16.3 is COMMIT. - `MARK: Open / Lock owner (§3.3.6 / §8.1.2)` → `§2.2.13 open_owner4 / §2.2.14 lock_owner4`. §3.3 only has subsections .1-.3; §8.1 is Location Attributes. - `≤ 1024 bytes opaque per §16.16` → `opaque per §2.2.13 (NFS4_OPAQUE_LIMIT = 1024 in RFC 7531)`. The literal value 1024 is *not* in 7530 itself — it lives in 7531's XDR description.
### 8. NFSValueTypes.swift
- `MARK: File handle (§2.2.4 / §16.x)` → `§2.1 nfs_fh4 / §16.x`. - `≤ NFS4_FHSIZE per §2.2` → `per §2.1 (Table 1)`. - `MARK: State identifier (§8.1.3)` → `§2.2.16 / §9.1.4`. §8 is Multi-Server Namespace. - `12 bytes per §8.1.3 / NFS4_OTHER_SIZE` → `per §2.2.16 / NFS4_OTHER_SIZE`. - `anonymous stateid (§8.1.4.2)` → `§9.1.4.3`. Both anonymous and READ-bypass stateids live in §9.1.4.3 "Special Stateids". - `READ bypass stateid (§8.1.4.3)` → `§9.1.4.3`. - `MARK: Time (§2.2.4 nfstime4)` → `§2.2.1 nfstime4`. - `MARK: Object type (§2.2.4 nfs_ftype4)` → `§2.1 nfs_ftype4`.
### 9. ClientRegistry.swift
- `§16.33-§16.35 — clientid lifecycle` → `§16.33-§16.34 (SETCLIENTID / SETCLIENTID_CONFIRM) + §16.28 (RENEW)`. §16.35 (VERIFY) has nothing to do with clientid lifecycle. - The `§16.33.5` (line 56, SETCLIENTID IMPLEMENTATION) and `§16.34.5` (line 98, SETCLIENTID_CONFIRM IMPLEMENTATION) citations in the same file were verified directly against the RFC body and left untouched.
### 10. RPCConstants.swift
- `NFSv4 program identification (§1.4)` → `§3.1 + §14`. §1.4 is "Overview of NFSv4 Features" — it does not cover the program number. - `NFSv4 program callback identification (§1.4)` → `§14 + §16.33`. The callback program number is per-client and is announced via SETCLIENTID.
### 11. CLAUDE.md (current rules + work-log entries)
- line 82 (§4 RFC reference policy *example*) `§16.23 (WRITE)` → `§16.36 (WRITE)`. §16.23 is READ; the example must end on a section number that actually matches the cited op. - line 166 (work-log) `§16.1 의 nfs_opnum4` → `§14.4 / §16 의 nfs_opnum4`. - line 228 (work-log) "OPEN4_share_access 의 high bits (§16.16.4) 에 OPEN4_SHARE_ACCESS_WANT_*" → replaced with a factually correct note: RFC 7530's OPEN4args (§16.16.2) has no high-bit hint slot, and the `OPEN4_SHARE_ACCESS_WANT_*` bits were added in RFC 5661 (NFSv4.1). - line 255 (work-log) `§5.8 attr 표 (lines 2200–2310)` → `§5.6/§5.7 attr 표 (REQUIRED + RECOMMENDED, lines ~2225–2310)`. The actual line range covers §5.4-§5.7, and the attribute *tables* live in §5.6 (REQUIRED) and §5.7 (RECOMMENDED).
### 12. Test files
- `Tests/NanoNFSTests/FATTRTests.swift:7` Suite name `(§5, §16.18)` → `(§5, §16.7)` (GETATTR). - `Tests/NanoNFSTests/CompoundDispatcherTests.swift:167` Suite name `(§16.2)` → `(§15.2)`. - Same file, line 326 `OPENATTR (§16.19, …)` → `(§16.17, …)`. §16.17 is OPENATTR; §16.19 is OPEN_DOWNGRADE.
### 13. NFSv4Constants.swift `NFSStatus` raw-value shift fix (user follow-up request)
Initially reported in `` as out of audit scope, but the user explicitly asked to fix the 1-slot shift in the 10037–10043 range as part of the same task.
| RFC 7530 §13.1 table | Old code | New code | | --- | --- | --- | | NFS4ERR_LOCKS_HELD = 10037 (§13.1.8.6) | `lockNotGranted = 10037` (name not in RFC 7530) | `locksHeld = 10037` | | NFS4ERR_OPENMODE = 10038 (§13.1.8.9) | `lockOldStateid = 10038` (name not in RFC 7530) | `openMode = 10038` | | NFS4ERR_BADOWNER = 10039 (§13.1.11.2) | `openMode = 10039` (name vs raw mismatch) | `badowner = 10039` | | NFS4ERR_BADCHAR = 10040 (§13.1.7.1) | `badowner = 10040` | `badchar = 10040` | | NFS4ERR_BADNAME = 10041 (§13.1.7.2) | `badchar = 10041` | `badname = 10041` | | NFS4ERR_BAD_RANGE = 10042 (§13.1.8.1) | `badname = 10042` | `badRange = 10042` | | NFS4ERR_LOCK_NOTSUPP = 10043 (§13.1.8.7) | `badRange = 10043` (name was meant to be BAD_RANGE) | `lockNotSupp = 10043` |
Impact analysis: - The only case actually used is `.badowner` (3 sites in `CompoundDispatcher.swift` lines 425/741/919 — owner-string parse failure paths in SETATTR / CREATE / OPEN). Before the fix the wire would emit `10040 (NFS4ERR_BADCHAR)` instead — macOS clients were receiving "bad character" instead of "bad owner". **The fix changes wire behaviour into RFC compliance — this is more than a cosmetic label tweak.** - `lockNotGranted` and `lockOldStateid` are names that do not appear in RFC 7530 at all and were not referenced anywhere in the codebase. They were quietly removed by re-using their slots for the real RFC names `locksHeld` / `openMode`. - `lockNotSupp = 10043` corresponds to `NFS4ERR_LOCK_NOTSUPP` in RFC 7530 §13.1.8.7. The shift fix freed up the slot and let us add the previously missing case at the same time. - The `NFSError → NFSStatus` mapping (`asStatus` extension) only references cases whose raw values were already correct (e.g. `.lockRangeOverlap → .lockRange`), so it is unaffected.
Verification: - `swift build` → success. - `swift test` → 65 tests passed in 10 suites.
## Build / test verification (overall)
- `swift build` → success. - `swift test` → 65 tests passed (same count as before, no regressions). - The citation-only changes have no behavioural effect (the only externally visible difference is the renaming of two test suites to cite the correct RFC sections). - The `NFSStatus` raw-value shift fix *does* change wire semantics — currently exercised by exactly one call site (`.badowner`).
### 14. CLAUDE.md §4 process rule hardening (user follow-up request)
User proposal: "to prevent hallucinations, work involving NFS spec must always look up the RFC 7530 document and cite the section / location in source code." The audit results themselves are evidence that the absence of such a rule led to accumulated hallucinations across the codebase, so the proposal was applied as written.
The existing §4 second bullet ("When the user references or quotes a specific section of `docs/rfc7530.txt`, **read that section directly** before responding") only fired *when the user explicitly referenced an RFC section*. It did not constrain the agent's *write path* — i.e. when an agent invents a `§16.X` citation from memory while authoring code. That gap is exactly how the 95+ citations audited here ended up wrong.
New rule (prepended as the first bullet of §4): - **Mandatory direct lookup in `docs/rfc7530.txt` before writing any new RFC 7530 citation.** Memory, prior training data, and analogy from other NFS RFCs (5661 / 3530) are all explicitly disallowed. If the citation cannot be positively verified, either grep the RFC for the relevant op / struct / error name first or do not write the citation at all. - The three traps repeatedly observed during this audit are pinned inline: 1. **Op number ↔ §16 section number offset** (op N = §16.(N-2), N=3..39). Five worked examples included (ACCESS / COMPOUND / GETATTR / READ / WRITE). 2. **Data-type locations**: `stateid4`, `nfstime4`, `change_info4`, `nfs_fh4`, `verifier4`, `open_owner4`, `lock_owner4`, etc. are defined in §2.1 or §2.2.X, *not* in §3.3.X / §8.1.X. (Both bogus chapters were observed in this audit.) 3. **NFSv4.1 (RFC 5661) features misattributed to 7530**: `OPEN4_SHARE_ACCESS_WANT_*`, `NFS4ERR_WRONG_TYPE`, `SECINFO_NO_NAME`, `NFS4ERR_LOCK_NOTGRANTED`, etc. do not exist in 7530. When in doubt, grep first.
With this rule in place, future-session agents cannot skip the lookup step at write time, which means a large post-hoc audit like this one should not have to be repeated.
Verification: - No `swift build` impact (rule-only change). - Touched: `CLAUDE.md` §4 (rule body) + the 2026-05-09 entry in §7 (decision record).
## What was deliberately *not* changed
- `RFC 4506` (XDR) and `RFC 5531` (ONC RPC) citations are outside the direct scope of this audit (which was tied to `docs/rfc7530.txt`). The existing `RFC 5531 §9 / §11 / §A.2 / §8.2` citations in code map onto the well-known structure of ONC RPC and were judged to be sound at a glance, so they were left as-is. - Per the CLAUDE.md §0 rule "Higher items win on conflict", work-log entries (2026-05-03 ~ 2026-05-08, in Korean) are point-in-time records. However, four clearly wrong RFC citations there would mislead future sessions and were corrected (see §11 above). The surrounding narrative was preserved.

# Findings outside the audit scope (for reference)
- `change_info4.atomic = false` with `before == after` (around CompoundDispatcher.swift:854) had its RFC citation corrected, but the underlying weakness in atomic-change verification still stands. It is already noted under "next work" in the 2026-05-03 work-log entry, so no separate tracking ticket was created here. - The CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03 note "NFS4ERR_LOCK_NOTSUPP (raw 가 같을 위험)" was itself factually off — the raw values are 10043 vs 10044, never colliding. With the present fix `NFS4ERR_LOCK_NOTSUPP = 10043` is now properly defined, so the original concern is moot.
